blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: In-situ conservation involves protecting species within their natural habitats, such as National Parks, Wildlife Sanctuaries, and Biosphere Reserves.
Ex-situ conservation safeguards threatened species outside their natural habitats using Botanical Gardens, Zoological Parks, Seed Banks, and Cryopreservation.
The Wildlife Protection Act of 1972 provides the legal framework for protecting species and establishing protected areas in India.
Biosphere Reserves follow a three-tier zoning system comprising Core, Buffer, and Transition zones to balance conservation and human development.
India hosts 4 major biodiversity hotspots: Himalayas, Western Ghats, Indo-Burma region, and Sundaland.

blocks.content: In-situ conservation protects species in their natural habitats, whereas ex-situ conservation safeguards them outside their natural environments.

items: Categorization of methods into In-situ (National Parks, Sanctuaries, Sacred Groves) vs Ex-situ (Botanical Gardens, Cryopreservation, Gene Banks) is a frequently asked MCQs area.
Understand the Biosphere Reserve zones: Core Zone permits no human activity, Buffer Zone permits limited research/education, and Transition Zone permits sustainable human settlements.
Memorize key environmental acts and years: Wildlife Protection Act (1972), Forest Conservation Act (1980), Environment Protection Act (1986), and Biological Diversity Act (2002).
